newsitem.title: UK: EMI shares rise on special share issue.
newsitem.headline: EMI shares rise on special share issue.

text.p: Shares in EMI Group Plc rose on Tuesday as the music publishing group unveiled plans for a 499 million stg capital distribution and a share split.
From being down 12-1/2p before the announcement, EMI shares were up 19p at 11.86 stg by 0856 GMT in volume of 518,457 shares.
The company said the distribution would be funded by extra borrowing and would take the form of a special one-for-one issue of "B" shares, redeemable by the company and valued at 114.5p.
It said the two-for-one share split should improve the marketability of the stock.
EMI said it had concluded that a higher level of debt funding would reduce its overall cost of capital and therefore boost shareholder value.
Dealers and analysts welcomed the distribution but said a cash handout had been expected.

"I don't think this is a surprise," said Nigel Reed, analyst at Paribas Capital Markets. "We were expecting some sort of return of cash, but it does suggest they don't need the cash for anything else and it makes good sense to keep the balance sheet in good order."
Separately EMI also said it had repurchased 120,000 shares at 11.70 stg, under an authority gained at last year's annual general meeting.
By 0950 GMT the stock was up 11-1/2p at 11.78-1/2 stg in volume of just under one million shares.
